key_insight: Agreement in annual capacity factor can mask substantial differences in predicted offshore wind wakes across locations, seasons, and atmospheric regimes.
engineering_relevance: Regional wind-energy assessments should account for wake-model sensitivity when estimating production from a 100.7 GW North Sea build-out.
method: Evaluate a 2050 offshore wind scenario under year-round weather conditions.
Compare HARMONIE-AROME mesoscale simulations, ASPIRE large-eddy simulations, and three engineering wake models.
Assess wake predictions across downstream distance, wind speed, and atmospheric stability.
evidence_signal: LES and mesoscale simulations accurately represent observed local free-stream winds, while all three engineering models predict higher monthly mean wind speeds than LES, with biases reaching 0.60–0.70 m/s at 10–40 km downstream.
watch_item: Validation against local free-stream observations does not establish wake accuracy across the full region; engineering-model biases also depend on atmospheric regime.
paper_title: Wake effects in a 100 GW North Sea offshore wind scenario: a model intercomparison under year-round weather conditions
